acceptance: Every affected test passes with get_available_memory_gb patched to 0.5 GB for the whole session (run once locally through the lock and report the command and result).
The same tests still pass with the real host reading.
At least one existing or new test still fails closed: a run whose estimate exceeds the pinned available memory raises InsufficientMemoryError.
The PR lists each changed test and why it runs a real benchmark.
description:
## Problem
Integration tests that run a real Polars benchmark through MCP or the CLI fail with InsufficientMemoryError when the host is busy, because the memory guard reads the host's live free memory. Seen 2026-11-24 in pr-preflight on two consecutive runs: tests/integration/test_execution_engine_recording.py::test_mcp_run_benchmark_records_requested_engine_and_collect_kwargs (both cases; also fails on develop code) and tests/integration/test_cli_mcp_result_parity.py::test_dataframe_runs_record_host_load_samples_from_both_entry_points[polars-df]. These tests are about engine recording and result parity, not about memory, so their outcome must not depend on other processes on the host.

## Decision gate
Choose one mechanism and apply it to every affected test: (a) a shared fixture that pins the guard's available-memory reading (get_available_memory_gb) to a fixed value large enough for the run, or (b) passing the existing ignore-memory-warnings option through the test's entry point. Default: (a), because it keeps the guard on the code path. Find every affected test by searching tests/ for real DataFrame runs through run_benchmark, benchbox run or the dataframe benchmark mixin; list them in the PR.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create), never the primary clone; heavy test runs only through lock-taking entry points; never set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK or force admission; stage explicit paths; add a changelog.d fragment if users can see the change; no explanatory comments (make comment-policy-check). Do not disable the guard in a global conftest, do not change the guard's product behaviour in this item (that is dataframe-memory-guard-overstates-small-runs-20261124), and keep at least one test that proves the guard refuses a real shortage.
